      - [CLAIM-347](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) — Frustration among an organization's demands is an ordinal fact before it is a quantity: the jointly satisfiable sets of demands form a downward-closed complex whose minimal non-faces are the minimal conflicts, relief is strict enlargement of that complex for the same declared demands, reorganizations that relieve different conflicts are incomparable, and dropping or suppressing a demand is not relief *(Proposed)*
        - [CLAIM-361](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-361.md) — Relief of an organization's frustration must be judged for an identified organization against a fixed reference set of its original demands, under an explicit correspondence between earlier and later demands: a demand excised or suppressed has changed the comparison and has not been satisfied, an endogenous revision of what the organization maintains is a transformation of it and not relief, and learning can change which processes bear the demands *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-284, CLAIM-287
        - [CLAIM-365](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) — On a norm-ball update set the local frustration residual Φ_r = min over ‖d‖ ≤ r of max_i(ε_i + g_iᵀd) equals the maximum over the simplex of Σλ_iε_i − r‖Σλ_ig_i‖_*, so infeasibility of the declared improvements has a certificate, and any admissible actual update exceeds Φ_r by a nonnegative governance regret *(Active)*
          - [CLAIM-357](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) — The frustration residual and governance regret separate structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and identify none of them as thwarting: a positive residual says no admissible update meets every declared requirement, a positive regret only that the actual update's worst residual exceeds the best achievable, which can hold while every requirement is met, and actual violation needs regret above the negative residual; aggregate performance does not tell infeasibility from realized violation, and the multipliers that certify infeasibility are not the weights governance assigns *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-368
- [CLAIM-050](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md) — Fidelity is relative to the communicative decisions the receiver must make, and Blackwell's order of experiments makes that comparison precise *(Proposed)*

  - [CLAIM-115](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) — What survives translation is the set of communicative distinctions and relations a receiving system can still reconstruct and act upon, not the wording or the proposition *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-061, CLAIM-082
    - [CLAIM-078](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-078.md) — The theory succeeds if its observational and decision measures predict changes of communicative identity that text similarity misses and follow its compositional predictions across reconstructions; it needs neither quantum contextuality nor exact Noether laws *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-126](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-126.md) — Model stitching tests whether a transport preserves decision-relevant information only in its reconstruction form: a map fitted to reproduce the target representation certifies one direction of Blackwell sufficiency, while task-loss stitching compares one decision problem through a fixed head, and a failure to stitch is no evidence against sufficiency *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-268
  - [CLAIM-220](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md) — For a named population of receivers and a stated family of tasks, what survives a translation, retelling or rendering is the set of task-relevant communicative distinctions those receivers can still recover from it, and measured preservation of the pragmatic observables predicts that recovery better than preservation of the wording or of the proposition, with or without its force *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-061

  - [CLAIM-348](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) — No coarse-graining is normatively adequate in general because it preserves stability, prediction or aggregate performance: a description adequate for an institution's performance can merge states its members' claims must distinguish, so adequacy is fixed by the evaluative target, and the target cannot be justified by the description that preserves it *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-152, CLAIM-350
- [CLAIM-061](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md) — Renderings that share a loose situation model can differ in footing and illocutionary force, so preserving the proposition is neither necessary nor sufficient for preserving the communicative event *(Proposed)*

  - [CLAIM-257](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-257.md) — Observational distortion should be summed over the contexts both covers can host, with the target's new questions asked of the source too, and the questions only one side can decide reported as a separate change of cover, so that a rendering that adds a relation pays for it *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-079](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-079.md) — Stability does not entail viability: a system can occupy a stable regime while losing access to trajectories that keep satisfying its constraints *(Active)*
- [CLAIM-080](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-080.md) — The agent is independently warranted: the account asks how a given agent's practical efficacy is organized, not what makes something an agent *(Active)*

    - [CLAIM-059](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-059.md) — Repeated reconstruction chains fall into different regimes under conditions assigned in advance, contracting toward conventions, accumulating neutrally or amplifying, and amplification needs a metric other than total variation, an enlarged state or state-dependent dynamics *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-267
    - [CLAIM-068](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-068.md) — Repeated reconstruction is attraction toward conventional regions of communicative possibility: pragmatic stances, not only lexicon and grammar, can be stabilized by transmission *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-090
    - [CLAIM-081](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-081.md) — Retaining information about the ancestor and drifting in the population's distribution are different profiles: a chain can forget where it started while staying far from the original, so convergence is not preservation and transmission is not degradation *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-270
      - [CLAIM-225](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-225.md) — Blackwell's order measures what an ideal decision-maker could do, not what a given receiver can reconstruct, and the line's claims that a rendering can improve access describe garblings that real receivers do better with, which is the shape of the Blackwell thesis's own defeat condition *(Active)* — also rests on CLAIM-087
    - [CLAIM-114](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-114.md) — Drift along a reconstruction chain can be marked by a pragmatic phase change, the first generation at which a different communicative configuration dominates, which per-step error does not show *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-101](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-101.md) — Translation is a context-conditioned transport process that preserves selected structures of communicative meaning to varying degrees while introducing distortions that may accumulate, attenuate or amplify under composition *(Superseded)*
  - [CLAIM-128](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) — No single ranking of translations holds across tasks: where distortion profiles trade off, only a task's priorities rank them, and the theory of fidelity fixes no weighting *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-371
- [CLAIM-112](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-112.md) — The operational account does not say that meaning is nothing but observable behaviour, nor that no stable content exists because interpretation is context-dependent *(Active)*

  - [CLAIM-074](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-074.md) — Fidelity is relative to the interpreter's learning history: a frame given in context is transient while an adaptation to it persists, so fidelity under a fixed interpreter, across interpreters and across states of adaptation are different quantities *(Proposed)*

    - [CLAIM-226](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md) — The defeat tests pool unnamed judges and treat their disagreement as noise, though the theory makes the act partly constituted by its audience; for historical sources there is no source audience at all, and for interlingual ones population differences are read as distortion *(Active)* — also rests on CLAIM-151
    - [CLAIM-244](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md) — The defeat tests take one holistic, task-free judgement of fidelity as ground truth, though the line's own theses say fidelity is task-relative, interpreter-relative and not a single ranking *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-106, CLAIM-128
    - [CLAIM-258](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md) — Blackwell's order compares experiments about one parameter, so it does not reach the normal translation case: source and target readers decide about situations with changed coordinates, and where the state is common a translator with context knowledge yields a rendering that is not a garbling of the source, which the order typically leaves incomparable with it and about which the direction the manuscript uses is silent *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-091, CLAIM-323

- [CLAIM-135](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-135.md) — Recovering latent structure from relational data is three achievements, reconstruction, identification up to stated ambiguities, and constitution of a communicative kind, and identifiability theory reaches the second at most *(Proposed)*

  - [CLAIM-223](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-223.md) — Whether a distinction survived is fixed by what the receivers can recover, and whether it can be shown to have survived is fixed by what the analyst's probes can identify, so the manuscript's thesis and the October fidelity clause, read so, answer different parts of one question *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-150](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-150.md) — Identification is not constitution: neither the Yoneda lemma, nor the invariance of a character, nor predictive or interventional success shows that relations constitute what a communicative act is, because an ontology of intrinsically individuated objects with relational properties can reproduce the same predictions *(Active)*

  - [CLAIM-157](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md) — Relative to a stated target, a combined form is one system while its joint dynamics are nearly decomposable with the form as a block whose gap beats the Occam factor, and it lasts as long as that block persists; the unit is the gap-isolated block, not any member *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-154, CLAIM-164
    - [CLAIM-174](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) — A candidate factor is an agent at a level when it is one system there, when a goal-directed description beats a device description by more than the Occam cost, and when its policy would adapt if its actions' consequences changed; it is a willed agent when, further, a will-organization over several regimes describes it better than none, and what passes that is the jurisdiction of a will-organization *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-154
      - [CLAIM-367](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md) — Whether a training-time regulatory condition belongs to a network depends on which unit is individuated for the training dynamics and whose jurisdiction governs the updates; in conventional training most of that governance falls to the optimizer–model–data system, so a condition of training is not thereby a condition of the network *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-027, CLAIM-152, CLAIM-170
- [CLAIM-154](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) — A candidate structure is worth naming as a unit when its effect-to-noise ratio outruns the Occam cost of keeping it: reify when d'² exceeds the log prior-to-posterior variance ratio *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-332](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-332.md) — A loosely organized population can change what an outside institution does through its members' separately motivated acts of making, selecting and passing things on, without forming a collective intention or judgment, when the organized pattern of those acts, and not only the acts of identifiable individuals, earns its place in explaining the change *(Proposed)*

  - [CLAIM-162](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) — Flow is intrapersonal synchronization: when an activity's immediate reward and its longer-run value coincide, no interest has to be overridden, and that is why focused action in flow is reported as effortless *(Proposed)*

- [CLAIM-177](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) — An argument developed with collaborators who keep no memory fails at identity, not at structure: concepts are redefined silently, objections and readings come back as though new, and the thesis changes without anyone arguing for the change *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-178](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-178.md) — A manuscript should be a view over the argument and not its only copy: a draft written straight from an exchange drops commitments and changes its thesis without saying so, and both become visible only against a record where claims carry status and inclusion separately *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-324

    - [CLAIM-182](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md) — Storage is not anchoring, addressability is: a structure that is kept but cannot be pointed at part by part does not stop re-derivation, and the same content becomes an anchor once its parts get addresses *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-177
      - [CLAIM-180](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-180.md) — Drift is retrieval failure outside a critical distance: a restatement close enough to an idea retrieves it, one that has drifted too far is taken for new, and a code bypasses retrieval by content altogether *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-177
      - [CLAIM-191](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-191.md) — Restating an argument across memoryless sessions is iterated transport with only a weak channel back to the source: without anchors, restatements drift toward the collaborators' own framings rather than at random, and a code restores continuity of transmission *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-002, CLAIM-177, CLAIM-267, CLAIM-270
    - [CLAIM-195](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-195.md) — For an argument, the constraint set that persistence is relative to is fixed by an amendable decision, not discovered: the record stipulates what counts as the same claim persisting, which makes the choice explicit without making it non-arbitrary *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-079
  - [CLAIM-186](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md) — How fast an argument grows sets how it grows: drift tracks how fast new material arrives relative to how fast it is anchored, so a fast, prolific exchange branches, as a crystal grown far from equilibrium does, and a project memory stabilizes an argument by keeping anchoring up with arrival *(Proposed)*

  - [CLAIM-190](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-190.md) — The anchoring measures are computed in the grammar that shapes the argument, so by themselves they cannot certify that drift fell: drift must also be judged under standards the record did not supply *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-264, CLAIM-266

- [CLAIM-263](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-263.md) — Whether two trained networks compute the same way can be tested by quotienting the architecture's full symmetry group and measuring what remains: a barrier that survives alignment marks a different mechanism, connection after alignment means shared feature structure, and the test cannot run where features have no counterpart *(Proposed)*

- [CLAIM-264](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) — Two objects can agree on every probe in a restricted family without being isomorphic, so equivalence under a probe family is coarser than identity unless the family is rich enough *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-322](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-322.md) — Agreement under a probe family is evidence that two objects share structure only to the degree that the family was chosen independently of the comparison and is evaluated on cases it was not chosen on, so a family selected to make two objects look alike shows only that it can be selected *(Proposed)*
    - [CLAIM-142](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md) — Two communicative realizations can agree on every probe in a restricted family without being structurally identical, so observational equivalence is relative to the probes, and only independently justified probes evaluated on held-out cases are evidence that structure was preserved *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-011, CLAIM-046, CLAIM-264
      - [CLAIM-129](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-129.md) — A factorization recovers only the structure visible in the relations it is fitted to, so a topic can survive a transformation that changes the communicative act, and a kind must be tested against probe families chosen for their bearing on the act *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-004, CLAIM-061
      - [CLAIM-133](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-133.md) — Communicative identity is relational continuity under admissible transformation: translation transports relationally organized observational structure, correspondence fixes what can be compared, admissibility which transformations count, and fidelity which communicatively consequential distinctions remain recoverable *(Superseded)* — also rests on CLAIM-011, CLAIM-050, CLAIM-077, CLAIM-143
      - [CLAIM-139](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) — A communicative kind's identity is grounded in its relational organization rather than in any expression or encoding; statistical methods recover aspects of that organization from restricted observations, translation transports it, and fidelity is which independently identifiable, decision-relevant relational distinctions persist *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-050, CLAIM-077, CLAIM-135, CLAIM-151

      - [CLAIM-204](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md) — A communicative kind's identity is grounded in its relational organization, for which competent participants' uptake is the standard; statistical methods recover aspects of it from restricted observations; translation transports it; and what persists is what the receivers can still recover, of which the analyst can certify the independently identifiable part *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-050, CLAIM-077, CLAIM-135, CLAIM-151, CLAIM-217, CLAIM-223

- [CLAIM-270](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-270.md) — Retaining information about where a Markov chain started and staying close to the starting distribution are different properties: a chain can forget its initial state while its distribution stays far from where it began, so convergence is not preservation and losing information about the origin is not degradation *(Active)*
- [CLAIM-275](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-275.md) — An intervention can come before the interpretation it makes available, so in an organization of processes meaning, policy and influence co-evolve and none of them is simply upstream of the others *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-297](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md) — When an operator's authority is updated by how well it performs on the interpretation it helped make dominant, the coupled meaning and influence of an organization can amplify an initial interpretive advantage without any gain in fidelity to independent evidence *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-277
    - [CLAIM-336](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md) — The pragmatic-transport and will-organization lines describe one model, an organization of operators that act on a shared interpretive state under a context while allocating one another's influence: a frame is the context under which operators act, a judgement is the response they yield, an action-generating regime is an operator or coalition, and a will-organization is the dynamics that allocates influence among them *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-279, CLAIM-286
      - [CLAIM-338](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) — The selectivity active inference gives action, sampling what one expects to experience, is played in the coupled meaning–authority model by the authority space: influence decides which operators retrieve and so what the next judgement observes, which makes Friston's self-confirming sampling the model's authority-to-interpretation arrow and his agent a coupled loop run without independent scoring *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-297
    - [CLAIM-341](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-341.md) — The loop that keeps a lucid agent's model in touch with what it models runs between judgement and observation: each judgement reshapes the observer whose later observations it then judges, and action on the world is not part of that loop, so active inference's action–perception cycle misplaces where the agent is active *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-275
- [CLAIM-277](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md) — Durable authority among an organization's processes need not be a primitive: trust can be the temporal regularity of endorsement that policies earn by being right often, and the same loop entrenches whatever gained influence early *(Proposed)*

- [CLAIM-281](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-281.md) — Endorsement indexed by role lets a process empower another as a critic while opposing its preferred policy, so an organization that allocates authority by role can keep disagreement working inside it instead of sorting into factions *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-282](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md) — Forbidding self-endorsement does not stop an operator from amplifying its own authority: once endorsement can carry authority more than one hop, reciprocal and cyclic endorsements recycle it, and only one-hop allocation within an epoch makes an operator's authority independent of its own endorsements *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-375](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md) — Under one-hop allocation within an epoch, an operator that endorses an ally whose policy is nearer its own than the collective decision is raises how far its preferred policy is realized while its own authority stays fixed, so the two conditions of the endorsement scheme hold together *(Active)*
    - [CLAIM-285](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md) — An endorsement scheme that denies each operator control over its own authority can make delegation do work: rewarded for how far their preferred policies are realized and not for authority held, operators delegate to aligned others, and the two conditions need not be confined to one-hop allocation *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-282
- [CLAIM-283](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) — The precedence a motive claims over action and the authority the rest of the organization grants it are different quantities, and internal conflict is the gap between them *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-286](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-286.md) — Habit, akrasia, rumination, rigidity and insight can be modelled as regimes of one organization, in which processes transform shared meaning and allocate one another's influence, with trust, specialization and higher-level agency arising from its history and not imposed *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-287](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md) — What persists when a self persists through inactivity is the capacity to reinstate an organization, not its continuous running, and continuity of that kind can branch and merge, so it is not an identity relation *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-290](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-290.md) — A positive-definite kernel's minimal realizations are unique up to a unitary, and two finite representation matrices with the same centred Gram matrix differ by a translation and an orthogonal map *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-379](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-379.md) — On a finite set of stimuli, regularized linear readouts with ridge b > 0 cannot tell apart two centred representations of the same width exactly when one is an orthogonal transformation of the other, and the unregularized CCA member cannot tell apart representations with the same column space, which differ by an invertible linear map *(Active)*
    - [CLAIM-269](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md) — A regularized linear readout can tell apart only representations that differ in normalized kernel, and kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed, so any distinction beyond that is supplied by the analyst, not by the readouts *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-317](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-317.md) — Self-presentations that differ by audience do no harm while the audiences are kept apart; people keep them apart and script the occasions where they must meet, and broadcast and networked media bring them together unchosen, which is when the presentations collide *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-318](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-318.md) — Within a shared observational scenario, exact structure-preserving symmetries are the invertible members of a nested family of stochastic transports, and among Markov kernels between finite sets the invertible ones are the permutation matrices, so the invertible core is the relabellings, a groupoid in which objects joined by an arrow have isomorphic automorphism groups *(Active)*
- [CLAIM-320](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-320.md) — Within one fixed measurement scenario, two no-signalling empirical models can agree on all but one of their contexts and on every single-observable marginal while their contextual fractions are 1 and 0, so keeping most local judgement distributions does not fix their global compatibility *(Active)*
- [CLAIM-323](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-323.md) — Where source and rendering are experiments about one common situation, a rendering that depends on the situation other than through the source is not a garbling of it and can be incomparable with it in Blackwell's order: with Z uniform on {1, 2, 3}, a source that tells whether Z = 1 and a rendering that tells whether Z = 3 each have the lower 0–1 risk on one of the problems of saying whether Z = 1 and whether Z = 3, so neither dominates *(Active)*
- [CLAIM-324](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-324.md) — In the What Survives Translation? exchange, the manuscript drafted straight from the crystallized argument changed the thesis with no turn arguing the move and dropped 24 of that argument's items, none on request, and the second crystallized argument announced its change of question but left items out without saying which had dissolved and which were lost *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-331](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md) — A level of organization has a temporal facet as well as a compositional one: higher-level variables are characteristically slower and longer-lived than the activity that produces them, though slowness is a mark of a level and not its definition *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-345](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-345.md) — Equal controllability rank does not fix the cost of control: for x_{t+1} = x_t + b·u the least quadratic effort for a displacement Δ is Δ²/b², unbounded as b → 0 while the system stays controllable, and in general the least effort is Δxᵀ W_T^† Δx, set by the Gramian and not by its rank *(Active)*
- [CLAIM-350](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md) — A coarse-graining preserves a deterministic judgment exactly when the judgment is constant on its fibres: the judgment then factors through the coarse description, uniquely on its image, and otherwise two states the judgment tells apart have been merged *(Active)*
- [CLAIM-371](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-371.md) — Under the componentwise order on distortion profiles, two profiles are incomparable exactly when they trade off, and then positive weightings can rank them either way, while every positive weighting agrees with a dominance *(Active)*

### From Interpretive framing operations generally do not commute, and this can be investigated without committing to quantum probability

- [CLAIM-052](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-052.md) — Interpretive framing operations generally do not commute, and this can be investigated without committing to quantum probability *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-117](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-117.md) — Pragmatic fidelity requires preserving the dynamics of interpretation, not only final judgements: a good transport approximately intertwines source and target framing operations *(Proposed)*
    - [CLAIM-063](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-063.md) — A transport that approximately intertwines each framing operation approximately preserves their commutator, so the degree to which interpretive perspectives interfere can itself be part of what a translation preserves *(Proposed)* — through [ARG-006](../record/arguments.d/ARG-006.md) — also rests on CLAIM-373
- [CLAIM-373](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-373.md) — If a map approximately intertwines two operators, with defects E_A = ΦA − A′Φ and E_B = ΦB − B′Φ, then Φ[A,B] − [A′,B′]Φ = A′E_B + E_A B − B′E_A − E_B A, so the commutator is carried to within (‖A‖ + ‖A′‖)‖E_B‖ + (‖B‖ + ‖B′‖)‖E_A‖ *(Active)*

### From Causal-loop consistency and sheaf contextuality are both local-to-global problems, but passing to distributions affects them oppositely: a loop with no deterministic solution has a distributional fixed point, while a model with no global section in its supports has no global distribution either

- [CLAIM-141](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-141.md) — Causal-loop consistency and sheaf contextuality are both local-to-global problems, but passing to distributions affects them oppositely: a loop with no deterministic solution has a distributional fixed point, while a model with no global section in its supports has no global distribution either *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-342](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) — What keeps a judgement–observation loop from confirming itself is evidence whose arrival or scoring does not pass through the interpretation it tests; action is one source of such evidence, not a necessary one, and a loop that selects its own evidence can lock in with action available *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-330
- [CLAIM-330](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md) — In the coupled meaning–influence model linearized at its symmetric state, with each field stable alone and nonnegative couplings, the coupling destabilizes symmetry exactly when βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ): only the loop can do it, and the direction that grows mixes meaning and authority *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-340](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md) — Scoring operators on predictions committed before the evidence is not by itself Regime B: in the linearized operator model the coupling of interpretation to endorsement has the sign of κ′ − κ̄, so commitment removes capture only when the interpretation bends the reading of the evidence no more than it bends the predictions, and it keeps the learning that revising after the evidence would lose *(Active)*
